questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting courses, mountains, nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: ETH Zurich provides a lot of information. It is almost too much but I think you can almost find the answer to any question you have in the material they provide.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Almost all communication and help was online. You have to participate in study start events for Erasmus students in the beginning where you are also overloaded with information. It is still very helpful though! I know it's possible to receive help from the "erasmus office" at ETH and as far as I know, they were very helpful to other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
The university offered student appartments to all erasmus students - it was very easy. 
However, there is a massive difference between the different dorms they offer, so you never know what you are gonna get. You shouldn't have too high expectations - it is not luxury but just normal student housing that is pretty affordable (compared to the general price level in Zürich) and gives you a good chance of meeting other exchange students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is no problem. As long as the apartment is in Zürich, public transport can take you anywhere in no time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to show up at an exchange office during the first week and register. As far as I remember, it was super easy and they were helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Online communication and meetings at the exchange office.
They are very busy the first couple of weeks, but I believe it is possible to receive the help you need.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
You can register for as many classes you want, try them out the first three weeks and then choose which classes you want to drop/keep. 
My recommendation is to register for too many classes, see what you like and choose based on your experience the first weeks of the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Dont stress too much. Read the information they send you, go to the office and then it should be fine. 

Register for too many classes and drop the ones you dont like (I think you get 3 weeks to do this)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teaching was not better than at KU but the courses are generally more specialized.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Both level and workload is a bit higher than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Similar teaching style.
The professors are approachable and willing to help with any problems you may have.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Computational Quantum Physics
2) Semiconductor Devices: Quantum Transport at the Nanoscale
3) Molecular and Materials Modelling
4) Ferromagnetism: From Thin Films to Spintronics
5) Electronic Transport in Nanostructures

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you want a very difficult course, I can recommend computational quantum physics. 
I personally liked "Molecular and Materials Modelling" and "Electronic Transport in Nanostructures" the best. The teachers are good and they are interesting if you like nanoscale physics and chemistry.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you want to travel around Switzerland in weekends and holidays (which you definitely have to do!), you will encounter very high costs of public transport. You absolutely have to get the "Half fare card" (costs around 1000kr) and gives you half price on all public transport for a year. If you dont get this, travelling will be way too expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is expensive. 
Restaurants and bars are also very expensive. 
Public transport

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: University sports is very big in Zürich. You can join up to 120 sports classes for free!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Parties, different types of events on campus (cinema, beer-week, ...). 
Theres an infinite amount of sports classes you can go to

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sports classes.
Find a good group of friends to go and enjoy the mountains (hiking, camping, skiing) 
Swimming in the river, lake

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Swiss mountains! There are so many amazing places. You will not get tired of going to the mountains!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not a problem. Everyone in the university environment are good at english and swiss people are similar to danes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Approach them, ask them about stuff. They will not go and talk to you if you dont approach them first. 
Just do it!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The local students work harder than what I'm used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I enjoyed nature more than culture. 
I had a feeling that everything just works in Switzerland which was pretty nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) you will receive a lot of information. Go through it slowly and make some "to do lists" to get your head around it. Dont worry if you miss a detail. You can get a lot of help once you arrive. 
2) Make sure to apply for funding! Switzerland is expensive and it is very nice not having to think about money all the time. 
3) Register for way too many courses (way too many ECTS) and drop the courses you dont like within the first 3 weeks of the semester. 
3)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of people from all over Europe and just enjoying being in a beautiful country with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Pressure and stress from university. I think the courses can seem very difficult but in the end it was honestly not that bad. The exams were fine and I think that if you just follow the lectures and study decently for the exams, you will be fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
